subject.title: [Bug]: Trajectory files fed back as context cause unbounded token consumption and unexpected API billing

question: Is source-level trajectory/session filtering enough to close this billing report, or should it stay open until maintainers capture current-main Windows fresh-session provider proof?
rationale: The reported impact is high and cross-provider, but current main only gives source-level confidence; choosing the closure threshold for a billing-sensitive session-state path needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep open for focused proof
options.body: Require a current-main Windows or equivalent fresh-session run with prompt/context diagnostics or provider-token evidence before closing.

options.title: Close based on source guardrails
options.body: Accept the current trajectory sidecar filters and session transcript selection paths as sufficient evidence that the original bug is addressed on main.

options.title: Convert to targeted investigation
options.body: Keep the issue open but narrow it to a maintainer-owned investigation of provider prompt construction and startup token counts.

recommendation.title: Keep open for focused proof
recommendation.body: Require a current-main Windows or equivalent fresh-session run with prompt/context diagnostics or provider-token evidence before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining uncertainty is closest to current interactive startup/session behavior, and ml12580 has recent merged work on that surface.
